title: Condicionais mistas / Mixed conditionals
bridge: In Spanish, mixed conditionals are uncommon and often avoided by using simpler structures. In Portuguese, they are more natural and frequently used to express hypothetical situations that combine tense and mood. Note that Portuguese uses the future of the past (simple conditional) similarly to Spanish, but compound tenses and tense agreement may differ. Pay special attention to the use of the compound pluperfect subjunctive (había + past participle) instead of the pluperfect subjunctive in certain contexts.
rule: In Portuguese, mixed conditionals combine the condition in one tense (past or present) with the result in another (present or past). The typical structure is: 'Se + compound pluperfect subjunctive (tivesse + past participle) + , + future of the past (ia) + infinitive' for past conditions with present results. For present conditions with past results, 'se + imperfect subjunctive + , + teria + past participle' is used. Unlike Spanish, European Portuguese often uses the compound future of the past (teria + past participle) instead of the simple conditional in these cases. Remember that the verb 'ter' is used as an auxiliary (not 'haber'), and the particle 'se' can appear at the beginning or after the verb in inverted sentences.

concept_examples.text: Se tivesse estudado, estaria pronto agora.
concept_examples.translation: If I had studied, I would be ready now.
concept_examples.phonetic: sɨ tiˈvesɨ ʃtuˈdadu, iʃˈtaɾiɐ ˈpɾõtu ɐˈgoɾɐ

concept_examples.text: Se fosse rico, teria comprado essa casa.
concept_examples.translation: If I were rich, I would have bought that house.
concept_examples.phonetic: sɨ ˈfɔsɨ ˈʁiku, tɨˈɾiɐ kõˈpɾadu ˈɛsɐ ˈkazɐ

concept_examples.text: Se não tivesses dito isso, não estaria chateada.
concept_examples.translation: If you hadn’t said that, I wouldn’t be upset.
concept_examples.phonetic: sɨ nɐ̃w tiˈvesɨʃ ˈditu ˈisu, nɐ̃w iʃtɐˈɾiɐ ʃɐtiˈadɐ

concept_examples.text: Se soubesse nadar, teria ido à praia.
concept_examples.translation: If I could swim, I would have gone to the beach.
concept_examples.phonetic: sɨ soˈbesɨ nɐˈdaɾ, tɨˈɾiɐ ˈidu a ˈpɾajɐ

common_error.wrong: Si hubiera estudiado, estaría pronto agora.
common_error.correct: Se tivesse estudado, estaria pronto agora.
common_error.correct_alt: Se tivesse estudado, estaria pronto agora.
common_error.explanation: The typical error is using 'si' instead of 'se', and 'haber' instead of 'ter'. In Portuguese, 'si' means 'yes' (affirmation), and the auxiliary for compound tenses is always 'ter'. Additionally, 'hubiera' does not exist; 'tivesse' (compound pluperfect subjunctive) is used instead. Remember that 'estaria' (conditional) is conjugated the same way as in Spanish, but with the ending -ia instead of -ía.

levels.label: Condicionais mistas com condição no passado e resultado no presente
levels.translation: Mixed conditionals with past condition and present result

examples.original: Se tivesse comido, não estaria com fome.
examples.phonetic: sɨ tiˈvesɨ kuˈmidu, nɐ̃w iʃtɐˈɾiɐ kõ ˈfɔmi
examples.translation: If I had eaten, I wouldn’t be hungry.
examples.note: Here, the compound pluperfect subjunctive (tivesse + past participle) combines with the simple conditional (estaria) to express a past condition with a present effect.

examples.original: Se tivesses chegado cedo, verias o início do filme.
examples.phonetic: sɨ tiˈvesɨʃ ʃɨˈɡadu ˈsedu, vɨˈɾiɐʃ u iˈnisju du ˈfilmɨ
examples.translation: If you had arrived early, you would see the beginning of the movie.
examples.note: Observe the agreement: 'tivesses' (2nd person singular) and 'verias' (conditional). In Spanish, it is 'verías', but in Portuguese, 'ia' does not take an accent.

examples.original: Se o avião tivesse saído atrasado, perderíamos a reunião.
examples.phonetic: sɨ u ɐviˈɐ̃w tiˈvesɨ sɐˈidu ɐtɾɐˈzadu, pɨɾdɨˈɾiɐmuʃ ɐ ʁɐwniˈɐ̃w
examples.translation: If the plane had left late, we would miss the meeting.
examples.note: The verb 'perder' is conjugated as 'perderíamos' in the conditional. Pay attention to the nasalization of 'avião'.

levels.label: Condicionais mistas com condição no presente e resultado no passado
levels.translation: Mixed conditionals with present condition and past result

examples.original: Se fosses mais cuidadoso, não terias partido o copo.
examples.phonetic: sɨ ˈfɔsɨʃ majʃ kujˈðɐdozu, nɐ̃w tɨˈɾiɐʃ pɐɾˈtidu u ˈkopu
examples.translation: If you were more careful, you wouldn’t have broken the glass.
examples.note: Present condition (fosses) with past result (terias partido). Note that 'terias' is the compound future of the past.

examples.original: Se ela fosse médica, teria ajudado muitas pessoas.
examples.phonetic: sɨ ˈɛlɐ ˈfɔsɨ ˈmɛðikɐ, tɨˈɾiɐ ɐʒuˈdadu ˈmũjtɐʃ pɨˈsoɐʃ
examples.translation: If she were a doctor, she would have helped many people.
examples.note: Use of the compound future of the past (teria + past participle) for past results.

examples.original: Se conseguisses o emprego, terias ganho um bom salário.
examples.phonetic: sɨ kõsɨˈɡisɨʃ u ẽˈpɾegu, tɨˈɾiɐʃ ˈɡɐ̃ɲu ũ bõ sɐˈlaɾju
examples.translation: If you got the job, you would have earned a good salary.
examples.note: Note that 'ganho' is the irregular past participle of 'ganhar' (in European Portuguese).

examples.original: Tivesse eu mais tempo, teria viajado mais.
examples.phonetic: tiˈvesɨ ˈew majʃ ˈtẽpu, tɨˈɾiɐ viɐˈʒadu majʃ
examples.translation: If I had more time, I would have traveled more.
examples.note: Inversion places the subjunctive at the beginning, omitting 'se'. It is more common in written or formal language.

examples.original: Se calhar, se tivesse sabido, não teria feito isso.
examples.phonetic: sɨ kɐˈʎaɾ, sɨ tiˈvesɨ sɐˈbidu, nɐ̃w tɨˈɾiɐ ˈfɐjtu ˈisu
examples.translation: Perhaps, if I had known, I wouldn’t have done that.
examples.note: The expression 'se calhar' (perhaps) is used colloquially in European Portuguese and does not carry the conditional 'se'.

examples.original: Tenhos estado doente, teria ido à festa.
examples.phonetic: ˈtẽɲuʃ iʃˈtadu ˈdwẽtɨ, tɨˈɾiɐ ˈidu a ˈfɛʃtɐ
examples.translation: If I hadn’t been sick, I would have gone to the party.
examples.note: In this structure, the condition is expressed with the compound present perfect indicative, omitting 'se'. It is frequent in informal situations.

examples.original: Se nós tivéssemos dinheiro, teríamos comprado outra casa.
examples.phonetic: sɨ nɔʃ tiˈvɛsɨmuʃ diˈɲɐjɾu, tɨˈɾiɐmuʃ kõˈpɾadu ˈoɾɐ ˈkazɐ
examples.translation: If we had money, we would have bought another house.
examples.note: Note the tonic form of 'nós' and the agreement of the verb 'ter' in the subjunctive.

title: Voz passiva avançada / Advanced passive voice (gerunds, infinitives, modals)
bridge: In Spanish, we use 'ser + past participle' for the passive voice, but in Portuguese there are important nuances: 1) The passive with 'se' (impersonal particle) is much more common than in Spanish, and the verb agrees with the patient subject (e.g., 'Vendem-se casas' = 'Se venden casas'). 2) In the passive with 'ser', the past participle agrees in gender and number just like in Spanish, but be careful: in Portuguese, 'ser' is not used with 'estar' to form the passive of state (use 'estar + past participle' with a resultative meaning, just like in Spanish). 3) In constructions with modal verbs (poder, dever, etc.), the passive is formed with the modal followed by 'ser + past participle', but in Portuguese it is common to use the passive with 'ter de + ser + past participle' (tener que ser). 4) The passive gerund is formed with 'sendo + past participle' and is equivalent to 'siendo + past participle', but in Portuguese it is also used in progressive passive constructions (está sendo feito).
rule: The advanced passive voice in Portuguese is constructed with the auxiliary 'ser' (conjugated) + past participle, which agrees in gender and number with the patient subject. With modal verbs (poder, dever, ter de, haver de), the modal is placed in its conjugated form and the auxiliary 'ser' in the infinitive. To express ongoing actions, use 'estar + sendo + past participle'. With gerund: 'sendo + past participle' (siendo + past participle). With infinitive: 'ser + past participle' after a preposition. The passive with 'se' (impersonal particle) is used with transitive verbs and the verb agrees with the subject: 'vendem-se casas' (se venden casas), 'vende-se casa' (se vende casa). With 'se', if the agent is explicit, use the passive with 'ser' (e.g., 'A casa foi vendida pelo corretor'). Do not use the passive with 'ser' + 'estar' for states (use 'estar + past participle' with a resultative meaning).

concept_examples.text: Este projeto está sendo elaborado pela equipe.
concept_examples.translation: This project is being prepared by the team.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈeʃtɨ pɾuˈʒetʊ ˈɛstɐ ˈsẽdʊ ɪlɐbʊˈɾadʊ ˈpelɐ ɪˈkɨpɨ/

concept_examples.text: Os documentos devem ser assinados pelo diretor.
concept_examples.translation: The documents must be signed by the director.
concept_examples.phonetic: /uʃ dɔkuˈmẽtʊz ˈdẽvẽʊ seɾ ɐsĩˈnadʊz ˈpelʊ dʒiɾeˈtoɾ/

concept_examples.text: Sendo aprovado no exame, você poderá entrar na universidade.
concept_examples.translation: If approved in the exam, you will be able to enter the university.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈsẽdʊ ɐpɾoˈvadʊ nu ɪˈzɐ̃mɨ, voˈse podeˈɾa ẽˈtɾaɾ nɐ univɨɾsɪˈdadʒi/

common_error.correct_alt: A casa foi vendida ontem (passive with ser).
common_error.explanation: In Spanish, we say 'la casa está vendida' to indicate a state, but in Portuguese, to express a punctual action in the past, we use 'foi vendida' (ser + past participle), not 'está vendida' (which indicates a resulting state). The error occurs because in Spanish 'ser' and 'estar' are sometimes confused, but in Portuguese the passive of action is always formed with 'ser'.

examples.original: Os trabalhos devem ser entregues até sexta-feira.
examples.phonetic: /uʃ tɾɐˈbaʎuz ˈdẽvẽʊ seɾ ẽˈtɾegɨz ɐˈtɛ ˈʃeʃtɐ ˈfejɾɐ/
examples.translation: The assignments must be turned in by Friday.
examples.note: The modal 'dever' + 'ser + past participle' agrees with the subject 'trabalhos'.

examples.original: A proposta pode ser aceita pelo comitê.
examples.phonetic: /ɐ pɾuˈpɔstɐ ˈpɔdʒi seɾ ɐˈsejtɐ ˈpelʊ komiˈte/
examples.translation: The proposal can be accepted by the committee.
examples.note: The modal 'pode' is followed by 'ser' + feminine singular past participle agreeing with 'proposta'.

examples.original: Os resultados têm de ser publicados no site.
examples.phonetic: /uʒ ʁezuwˈtaduz ˈtẽj dʒi seɾ publikaˈdʊʒ nu ˈsitʃi/
examples.translation: The results have to be published on the website.
examples.note: The construction 'ter de + ser + past participle' expresses obligation, equivalent to 'tener que'.

levels.label: Passiva progressiva: estar + sendo + particípio
levels.translation: Progressive passive: estar + being + past participle

examples.original: As obras estão sendo realizadas no centro da cidade.
examples.phonetic: /ɐz ˈɔbɾɐz ɪsˈtɐ̃w ˈsẽdʊ ʁeɐlizaˈðaz nu ˈsẽtɾʊ dɐ sɪˈdadʒi/
examples.translation: The works are being carried out in the city center.
examples.note: Use of 'estar + sendo + past participle' for ongoing action. The past participle agrees with 'obras'.

examples.original: O relatório está sendo elaborado pela consultora.
examples.phonetic: /u ʁelaˈtɔɾiʊ ɪsˈtɐ ˈsẽdʊ ɪlɐbuˈɾadʊ ˈpelɐ kõsuˈtoɾɐ/
examples.translation: The report is being prepared by the consultant.
examples.note: Masculine singular agreement: 'elaborado'.

examples.original: As medidas estão sendo estudadas pelo governo.
examples.phonetic: /ɐʒ mɨˈðidɐz ɪsˈtɐ̃w ˈsẽdʊ ɪstuˈðadɐz ˈpelʊ ɡoˈveɾnu/
examples.translation: The measures are being studied by the government.
examples.note: The past participle 'estudadas' agrees in feminine plural with 'medidas'.

examples.original: Sendo informado dos fatos, ele poderá agir corretamente.
examples.phonetic: /ˈsẽdʊ ɪ̃foɾmˈadʊ duʃ ˈfatʊz, ˈelɪ puˈdɛɾɐ ɐˈʒiɾ koʁeˈtɐ̃mẽtʃi/
examples.translation: Being informed of the facts, he will be able to act correctly.
examples.note: Use of passive gerund 'sendo + past participle' with conditional/causal meaning.

examples.original: Ao ser concluído, o projeto será divulgado.
examples.phonetic: /ɐw seɾ kõkluˈidu, u pɾuˈʒetʊ sɛˈɾä dʒivuwˈɡadu/
examples.translation: Upon completion, the project will be announced.
examples.note: Passive infinitive with preposition 'ao' + 'ser + past participle'.

examples.original: A tem de ser resolvida a questão dos prazos.
examples.phonetic: /ˈa ˈtẽj dʒi seɾ ʁezɔwˈviðɐ ɐ kiʃˈtɐ̃w duʃ ˈpɾazuz/
examples.translation: The matter of deadlines has to be resolved.
examples.note: Construction with 'ter de' + passive infinitive; inversion may occur for emphasis.

title: Discurso indireto avançado / Advanced indirect speech
bridge: In Spanish, when switching to indirect speech, we adjust verb tenses and pronouns, but Portuguese adds nuances with the 'futuro do pretérito' (conditional) and 'futuro do presente' (simple future), which sometimes behave differently. Additionally, Portuguese uses the 'pretérito mais-que-perfeito composto' (had + past participle) more regularly than Spanish. Pay attention to changes from 'se' to 'si' and the placement of unstressed pronouns, which in Portuguese can come after the verb in certain tenses.
rule: In Portuguese, advanced indirect speech follows patterns similar to Spanish but with specific features: 1) When reporting statements, verb tenses shift: present → 'pretérito imperfeito', 'pretérito perfeito' → 'pretérito mais-que-perfeito composto', simple future → 'futuro do pretérito' (conditional). 2) For reporting indirect questions, 'se' (if/whether) is used, and the subject-verb order is maintained. 3) Personal and possessive pronouns change based on perspective: 'eu' → 'ele/ela', 'meu' → 'seu'. 4) In Portuguese, the 'futuro do pretérito' is used for both conditions and reporting future actions from the past. 5) With verbs like 'dizer' (to say), 'perguntar' (to ask), 'responder' (to answer), the conjunction 'que' is used for statements and 'se' for yes/no indirect questions. Exclamations are introduced with 'que' or 'como'. Remember that in Portuguese, unstressed pronouns in indirect speech are typically proclitic (before the verb) with conjugated verbs but can be enclitic with infinitives or compound tenses.

concept_examples.text: Ela disse que tinha terminado o trabalho.
concept_examples.translation: Ella dijo que había terminado el trabajo.
concept_examples.phonetic: ˈɛlɐ ˈdisi ki ˈtĩɲɐ tɨɾmiˈnadʊ u tɾɐˈbaʎu

concept_examples.text: Ele perguntou se nós iríamos à festa.
concept_examples.translation: Él preguntó si nosotros iríamos a la fiesta.
concept_examples.phonetic: ˈeli pɨɾɡũˈtow si nɔjz iˈɾiɐ̃w a ˈfɛʃtɐ

concept_examples.text: O professor explicou que o exame seria na próxima semana.
concept_examples.translation: El profesor explicó que el examen sería la próxima semana.
concept_examples.phonetic: u pɾufɨˈsoɾ ɐjʃpliˈkow ki u ɨˈzɐmɨ sɨˈɾiɐ nɐ ˈpɾɔsimɐ sɨˈmɐnɐ

common_error.explanation: In Spanish, the present tense is often maintained in indirect speech ('dijo que está cansada') when the fact remains true. In Portuguese, however, it is more common (and formally correct in advanced indirect speech) to shift the verb tense: the present 'está' becomes the 'pretérito imperfeito' 'estava'. This is a stricter rule than in Spanish, where the present is sometimes allowed. To avoid mistakes, always apply temporal agreement when reporting in Portuguese.

examples.original: Ele disse que estava doente.
examples.phonetic: ˈeli ˈdisi ki ɨʃˈtavɐ duˈẽtɨ
examples.translation: Él dijo que estaba enfermo.
examples.note: The present 'está' changes to the 'pretérito imperfeito' 'estava' when reporting in the past.

examples.original: Nós explicámos que tínhamos chegado tarde.
examples.phonetic: nɔjz ɐjʃpliˈkamuz ki ˈtĩɲɐmuʃ ʃɨˈɡadu ˈtaɾdɨ
examples.translation: Nosotros explicamos que habíamos llegado tarde.
examples.note: The simple 'pretérito perfeito' 'chegámos' becomes the compound 'pretérito mais-que-perfeito' 'tínhamos chegado'.

examples.original: Ela perguntou se eu queria café.
examples.phonetic: ˈɛlɐ pɨɾɡũˈtow si ew ˈkɛɾiɐ kɐˈfɛ
examples.translation: Ella preguntó si yo quería café.
examples.note: 'Se' (if/whether) is used for yes/no indirect questions, with the verb in the 'pretérito imperfeito'.

examples.original: O polícia perguntou onde estava o carro.
examples.phonetic: u puˈlisiɐ pɨɾɡũˈtow ˈõdɨ ɨʃˈtavɐ u ˈkaʁu
examples.translation: El policía preguntó dónde estaba el coche.
examples.note: Questions with interrogative words (onde, como, quando) maintain their order without inversion in indirect speech.

examples.original: Ele disse que viria se tivesse tempo.
examples.phonetic: ˈeli ˈdisi ki viˈɾiɐ si tiˈvɛsɨ ˈtẽpu
examples.translation: Él dijo que vendría si tuviera tiempo.
examples.note: The simple future ('virá') changes to the 'futuro do pretérito' ('viria') in indirect speech, just like the conditional in Spanish.

examples.original: A professora avisou que a prova seria difícil.
examples.phonetic: ɐ pɾufɨˈsoɾɐ ɐviˈzow ki ɐ ˈpɾɔvɐ sɨˈɾiɐ diˈfisiw
examples.translation: La profesora avisó que la prueba sería difícil.
examples.note: The 'futuro do pretérito' 'seria' is used to report a future action from the past, similar to the conditional in Spanish.
